problem: Text-based embodied planning benchmarks such as TextWorld and ALFWorld assume full observability and teleportation between semantic waypoints inside single small rooms. Visual simulators (Habitat/HM3D, iTHOR, ProcTHOR, ALFRED) instead use low-level geometric actions (MoveAhead/RotateLeft) that do not fit LLM/VLM interfaces and cannot be used by text-only models. As a result, nobody has measured how well LLM/VLM planners reason spatially under partial observability and limited reachability in multi-room homes.
motivation: LLMs and VLMs are widely used as high-level household task planners. Real homes, however, require the agent to explore frontiers, localize itself, and trade off navigation against interaction under reachability limits. The driving observation is that ALFWorld-style infinite reachability makes LLMs look strong (about 80–89% success) and hides a large spatial-reasoning deficit that only appears once reachability is constrained.
key_idea: Build a large ProcTHOR-derived, multi-room household benchmark with language-level, reachability-constrained actions (go to frontier / object / through door, interact with facing object within a configurable radius), in both a PDDL text mode and a ProcTHOR vision mode, then evaluate many LLMs/VLMs combined with in-context-learning agents on it.
insight: Reachability, not task-level planning, is the bottleneck. Averaged over 5 ICL methods, Qwen2.5-72B falls from 81.19% (infinite reach) to 38.03% (3m) and 19.12% (1.5m). ICL methods mainly improve planning rather than spatial reasoning: Reflexion is best, but its gains come from replaying episodes, saturate after about 3 reruns (Fig. 10), and stay under 30% at 1.5m. A dynamic topological map helps only marginally (average 14.02→14.45% at 3m, 6.08→6.73% at 1.5m); Table 2 shows it pushes agents toward more navigation actions rather than more efficient interaction. A VLM on raw images beats the same-size LLM given oracle-segmentation text (21.69% vs 19.66%). The text environment preserves the model ranking of the vision setting while being 7.8× faster, so it can serve as a cheap proxy.
method: PDDL text environment (built on TextWorld): predicates cover object states (isClean/isHot/isCool/isSliced/isOn…), containment (receptacleInReceptacle, objectInReceptacle, objectInObject, up to 4 nesting levels), location adjacency, rooms/doors and agent location. Transitions are deterministic, the reward is sparse on the goal predicates, and a Translator maps symbolic state to natural-language observations and NL actions back to symbolic actions. Initial states are extracted from ProcTHOR scenes.

Frontier waypoint graph: per-room frontier locations are sampled with Farthest Point Sampling so they are fully connected and visiting all of them covers the whole room. Doors connect rooms, and the agent can only stand at object or frontier locations.

Reachability constraint: the interaction/visibility radius is infinite (ALFWorld-style teleport), 3m or 1.5m. The partial settings come in map-based (dynamic topological map that allows direct return to previously visited locations) and map-free variants, giving 5 text conditions.

Vision mode on ProcTHOR: annotated egocentric 360° panoramas with frontier markers, object-centric RGB views and action-success flags, used for VLMs. A vision-LLM variant converts oracle depth plus instance segmentation into a voxel/2D map and ProcWorld-style text, with dynamic frontier navigation. The vision mode is run only at 1.5m with a map.

Unified discrete language action space: Go to Surrounding Object, Go to Frontier Location, Go Through Door, and Interact with Facing Object (pick, place, open, close, toggle, slice, heat, cool, clean). An episode fails if not solved within 50 steps.

Dataset: 16 ALFRED-style task types (including slice and two-level-containment variants), 84 object categories, 5,000 scenes (1–10 rooms, 6–243 objects, 1–42 frontiers), 10M evaluation variations and 1.2M tasks with expert demos. The validation set has 3,600 tasks from 50 scenes.

Evaluation harness: 12 open LLMs (Qwen2.5 0.5B–72B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Phi-3.5-mini, GLM-4-9B) × 5 ICL agents × 5 settings = 1,080,000 runs. The ICL agents are ReAct, AgentBench, ALFChat (AutoGen executor/assistant/grounding agents), StateFlow (re-implemented with an extended state machine) and Reflexion (on AgentBench, up to 5 reruns). Additional runs cover Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B/72B and GPT-4o (ALFChat, one setting).

setting.backbone: Frozen LLMs (Qwen2.5-0.5B…72B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B/3.2-3B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Phi-3.5-mini, GLM-4-9B-chat, GPT-4o) and VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B/72B-Instruct), driven by ICL agent frameworks (ReAct, AgentBench, ALFChat, StateFlow, Reflexion)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; in-context few-shot examples only). The benchmark provides 1.2M expert-demo tasks, but none are used for training in the paper.
setting.observation: Text mode: symbolic NL descriptions of visible objects with 2D coordinates, reachable frontier locations, doors, object states and containment relations (360° view). Vision mode: annotated 360° panoramas with frontier markers plus object-centric RGB views. Vision-LLM variant: text converted from oracle depth and instance segmentation.
setting.action_space: Discrete high-level language actions: go to frontier location / go to surrounding object / go through door / interact with facing object (pick, place, open, close, toggle, slice, heat, cool, clean). Interaction and visibility are limited by a radius (inf, 3m, 1.5m). 50-step budget.
setting.simulator: Custom PDDL/TextWorld text environment built from ProcTHOR scenes; ProcTHOR (AI2-THOR) for the vision mode
setting.privileged: Frontier waypoints, object coordinates, object states and containment relations are given symbolically (text mode). The vision-LLM variant uses oracle depth and instance segmentation. The infinite-reach setting allows teleportation, and the map-based settings provide a dynamic topological map of visited locations.

numbers_note: This is a benchmark paper with no proposed agent. The entries are the authors' own evaluations of existing ICL agents with frozen LLMs/VLMs on their new ProcWorld validation set (3,600 tasks). Complete per-model tables for all 12 LLMs × 5 ICL methods × 5 settings are in Appendix Tables 3–12 (SR as fractions, plus average steps), and Table 13 covers ProcTHOR visual-world alignment. Several results appear only in figures: Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B (Fig. 6a), per-ICL-method averages (Fig. 6b), per-task-type SR (Fig. 7) and Reflexion rerun curves (Figs. 10–11). The text also has inconsistencies: '500 distinct environments' vs '5000 scenes'; '12 LLMs and 1 VLM' vs '3 VLMs'; the GPT-4o table is referenced as Table 15 but printed as Table 14.
results: Constraining reachability collapses LLM planning. Reflexion + Qwen2.5-72B, the best text agent, reaches 88.7% SR with ALFWorld-style infinite reach but only 51.8% at 3m and 29.3% / 27.2% at 1.5m (map-free / map). Averaged over ICL methods, Qwen2.5-72B drops 81.19% → 38.03% → 19.12%. Across ICL agents, Reflexion > StateFlow ≈ ALFChat ≈ AgentBench ≈ ReAct, and larger Qwen models consistently do better (0.5B ≈ 0%). GPT-4o with ALFChat gets only 18.9% at partial(map, 1.5m), versus 16.9% for Qwen2.5-72B with ALFChat. Qwen2.5-VL-72B on raw images (21.69%) beats Qwen2.5-72B with oracle-segmentation text (19.66%).
limitations: Strong simplifications: 360° field of view, no collision or object-size physics in the text environment, simplistic ProcTHOR renderings, and no fine-grained manipulation.

The vision/VLM evaluation is thin: only the 1.5m map setting and the Qwen2.5-VL family. GPT-4o is evaluated only with ALFChat in one setting, and no fine-tuned agents are tested despite 1.2M expert demos.
Reporting is partly inconsistent (500 vs 5000 scenes; VLM count), and many results are given only in figures.
